answer: Agent networks can suppress Sybil attacks through radio distance bounding. Nodes exchange nanosecond pulses with anchored stations, such as a transceiver on a port wharf and another atop a local knoll. A protocol bridge evaluates these propagation delays to verify unique locations, forcing attackers to incur the verifiable cost of deploying discrete radio transceivers per identity. However, this architecture remains vulnerable to low-latency wormhole relays.
